executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify is a UK seed-stage climate tech company that has developed the HeatHub — a distributed edge data centre unit installed in homes to replace gas boilers, using waste heat from cloud computing workloads to provide free space heating and hot water. The company completed its first real-world residential pilot in Essex in December 2024 and is a named technology partner in the Ofgem SIF-backed SHIELD programme led by UK Power Networks.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Residential decarbonisation, gas boiler replacement, waste heat recovery, and fuel poverty alleviation are Thermify's strongest grant themes — perfectly aligned with UK government Net Zero heating priorities and Innovate UK's active Net Zero Heat programme. The novel convergence of distributed compute and residential heat also positions Thermify strongly for deep-tech innovation funds such as the EIC Accelerator.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: The UK is overwhelmingly the strongest funding geography given Thermify's exclusive operational presence there, the active Innovate UK and Ofgem SIF ecosystem, and the government's Warm Homes Plan driving substantial public investment in residential decarbonisation. The EU (via EIC Accelerator under Horizon Europe association) is the second priority as a high-value deep-tech route.
executive_summary.key_constraints: Thermify's two main barriers are: (1) many of the highest-value programmes (Ofgem SIF, Warm Homes Social Housing Fund) require a licensed network operator or housing association as lead applicant, limiting Thermify to consortium partner roles where it cannot receive funds directly; and (2) key programme windows (Net Zero Heat, NZIP successor) are in recurring but unconfirmed states, requiring active monitoring rather than immediate application.

Prior Innovate UK grant history and existing programme relationships strengthen the application profile significantly.
opportunities.strategic_value_explanation: A further Innovate UK Net Zero Heat award would validate Thermify's technology at programme level, strengthen its credibility profile for follow-on investment, and provide the financial runway to complete SHIELD rollout and begin commercial scaling.

opportunities.notes: This is a programme umbrella — a specific named competition must be open before applying. The most recently evidenced competition is the Net Zero Heat Innovation Lab. Thermify should set up alerts on the Innovate UK funding portal for new Net Zero Heat competitions.  Application window not currently open — this is a well-established recurring programme. Monitor for next round opening.
opportunities.reason_for_inclusion: Gas boiler replacement through novel low-carbon heat technology is the literal mandate of this programme, making Thermify's HeatHub the natural application candidate with the added benefit of an existing Innovate UK grant relationship.
opportunities.reason_for_caution: No specific open competition window is currently confirmed — this is a programme umbrella, so Thermify must monitor closely and be ready to apply within days of a new call opening, as windows are typically short (6–8 weeks).

opportunities.thematic_fit_explanation: Smart Grants fund disruptive innovation across all technology sectors including energy and deeptech, and Thermify's patent-backed compute-heat convergence system fits the 'game-changing R&D' framing; however, this is a horizontal programme rather than a sector-specific heat or decarbonisation call, requiring Thermify to frame its narrative around technological novelty rather than thematic alignment.
opportunities.strategic_value_explanation: Another Innovate UK award would reinforce Thermify's credibility and provide financial runway, but Smart Grants carry less sector-specific prestige than a Net Zero Heat award for this particular technology.

opportunities.notes: Smart Grants have multiple open rounds per year; the specific open competition must be identified on the Innovate UK portal. Best applied for if no sector-specific Net Zero Heat competition is open simultaneously, as that programme offers stronger thematic alignment.
opportunities.reason_for_inclusion: Thermify's novel compute-heat convergence system is a strong candidate for Innovate UK's cross-sectoral disruptive innovation mandate, with an existing grant relationship reducing application risk.
opportunities.reason_for_caution: As a horizontal programme assessed across all technology sectors, Thermify faces competition from a much wider pool of applicants and cannot rely on thematic alignment alone — the application must make an exceptionally strong case for commercial potential and technological novelty.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue the EIC Accelerator as the primary high-value deep-tech bet (start with the low-burden short application immediately when the 2026 window opens), while simultaneously monitoring Innovate UK's Net Zero Heat programme for the next open competition — this is the single strongest thematic match in the UK landscape given Thermify's TRL 6-7 and existing IUK relationship. Use the SHIELD/SIF consortium as proof of institutional validation in all applications.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: United Kingdom (primary — deepest thematic alignment, existing relationships, and direct programme access) and EU via Horizon Europe association (secondary — EIC Accelerator offers transformational funding and prestige for exactly this type of deeptech breakthrough).
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1. Innovate UK Net Zero Heat Programme — apply to the next open competition as lead SME applicant; 2. EIC Accelerator — submit a short application in the next 2026 window targeting Green Deal strand; 3. NZIP successor / Warm Homes Plan innovation fund — monitor DESNZ closely for announcement of successor programme.
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: Deepening the existing UK Power Networks / SHIELD relationship is critical — it unlocks future Ofgem SIF consortium bids. Proactively partnering with 2–3 housing associations already engaged through SHIELD will enable co-bidding on future Warm Homes Social Housing Fund waves. For EIC Accelerator, no formal consortium is required but an EU academic or research partner would strengthen the application narrative.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to build a quantified impact dataset from the Essex pilot and the wider SHIELD rollout (energy savings, carbon reduction, fuel poverty metrics per household) — this evidence base is essential for scoring highly on impact in Innovate UK and EIC applications. Financial forecasting and a clear commercialisation roadmap will also be required for EIC Accelerator's full application stage.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: The primary risk is timing uncertainty — Thermify's strongest programmes (Net Zero Heat, NZIP successor) have no confirmed open windows, and missing a window by even a week is disqualifying. A secondary risk is that Thermify's hybrid compute-heat model may confuse assessors unfamiliar with distributed edge computing, requiring strong communication of the primary residential decarbonisation outcome rather than the technology architecture.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify replaces domestic gas boilers by installing distributed edge data centre units ('HeatHubs') in or near homes, capturing waste heat from cloud computing to provide space heating and hot water at no energy cost to the homeowner.
company_profile.technology: Distributed edge data centre hardware (HeatHub) installed at residential premises that processes cloud computing workloads for business customers; waste heat generated by the compute process is captured via a heat-transfer system and routed into the home's central heating circuit, eliminating the need for conventional cooling and replacing gas boilers. The system is patent-backed and internet-connected for remote management.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Reduction in household energy bills (reported savings of ~£335/month in pilot) and elimination of gas boiler dependency, cutting residential carbon emissions from heating.
secondary_benefits: Eliminates active cooling energy consumption at conventional data centres
Provides low-cost or zero-cost heat to low-income and fuel-poor households
Offers businesses a greener, distributed colocation alternative to traditional data centres
Compatible with integration alongside solar panels, battery storage, and heat pump systems
company_profile.trl: TRL 6-7 — first real-world residential pilot completed (Essex couple, installed December 2024, covered by BBC and Daily Mail November 2025); broader social housing pilots planned under the SHIELD programme with UK Power Networks and Ofgem SIF funding; not yet at commercial scale deployment.
funding_characteristics: grant-backed (Ofgem Strategic Innovation Fund, Innovate UK)
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify is a UK climate tech startup that has developed the HeatHub — a compact, internet-connected distributed data centre unit installed at homes in place of a gas boiler. The unit processes cloud computing workloads for paying business customers, and the waste heat generated is captured and used to heat the home and hot water, meaning the same unit of energy does double duty. The company offers a parallel product, Thermify Cloud for Business, positioning distributed HeatHub nodes as an environmentally friendly colocation alternative.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify completed its first live residential pilot in Essex in December 2024, with the homeowners reported to be saving approximately £335/month on energy bills, generating significant UK press coverage including BBC News and the Daily Mail in November 2025. The company is a key technology partner in the Ofgem Strategic Innovation Fund-backed SHIELD project led by UK Power Networks, which aims to roll out distributed data centre heating to low-income and social housing residents, with Innovate UK co-support; a wider SHIELD roll-out was confirmed in October 2025. Thermify has run or is running an EIS-eligible equity crowdfunding campaign on Seedrs/Republic, and remains a very small team (2–10 employees) at early commercial stage.
